recruiter.title: Recruiter view
recruiter.intro: How a recruiter, and the applicant-tracking software in front of them, would screen your CV, with advice to improve it. All checks run on this PC.
recruiter.capped: The overall score is capped at {cap} because the file contains hidden text.
recruiter.readability.no_text: No text can be read from the CV: applicant-tracking software sees an empty document.
recruiter.readability.no_text.advice: Export the CV from Word, LibreOffice or Google Docs as a text PDF or as DOCX instead of scanning or photographing it.
recruiter.readability.image_file: The CV is a picture. Most applicant-tracking software cannot read text inside images.
recruiter.readability.image_file.advice: Send a text PDF or a DOCX. Keep the picture only if the job ad explicitly asks for it.
recruiter.readability.image_pages: {pages} page(s) of the PDF are images without readable text.
recruiter.readability.image_pages.advice: Recreate those pages as text (not scans) so that the software can read every page.
recruiter.readability.heading_missing.ex: No standard heading for work experience was found.
Add a plain heading such as "Work experience" so that the software files your jobs in the right place.
recruiter.readability.heading_missing.ed: No standard heading for education was found.
Add a plain heading such as "Education" before your degrees and diplomas.
recruiter.readability.heading_missing.sk: No standard heading for skills was found.
Add a "Skills" heading with the tools and abilities a recruiter will search for.
recruiter.readability.heading_missing.la: No standard heading for languages was found.
Add a "Languages" heading with each language and its level (for example B2).
recruiter.readability.headings_ok: All the standard section headings are present.
recruiter.readability.contact_email_miss: Put a professional e-mail address at the top of the first page, as plain text.
recruiter.readability.contact_phone_miss: Add a mobile number with the international prefix at the top of the CV.
recruiter.readability.contact_town_missi: Your town is not clear from the contact details.
Add your town (the street address is not needed): recruiters filter candidates by distance.
recruiter.readability.contact_linkedin_m: If you have an up-to-date LinkedIn profile, add its short address next to your contacts.
recruiter.readability.pages_too_many.adv: Bring it down to two pages: keep the last 10-15 years in detail and summarise older jobs in one line each.
recruiter.readability.pages_many.advice: Two pages are usually enough; consider shortening older or less relevant roles.
recruiter.readability.too_short: The CV is very short ({words} words; at least {minimum} are recommended).
recruiter.readability.too_short.advice: Describe what you did in each job, with tools, numbers and results: a short CV gives the software and the recruiter little to match.
recruiter.readability.too_long: The CV is long ({words} words; more than {maximum}).
recruiter.readability.too_long.advice: Cut repetitions and old details; recruiters spend less than a minute on the first read.
recruiter.readability.layout_fragmented: {share}% of the lines are one or two words: tables or columns may be read out of order.
Use a single-column layout without text boxes or tables for the main content.
recruiter.readability.broken_words: {count} words are split across lines with a hyphen.
recruiter.readability.broken_words.advic: Turn off automatic hyphenation so that keywords stay whole.
recruiter.readability.spaced_letters: {count} lines have letters spaced out (for example "S K I L L S").
recruiter.readability.spaced_letters.adv: Write headings as normal words and use bold or size instead of letter spacing.
recruiter.readability.odd_characters: {count} unreadable characters were found (missing fonts or symbols).
recruiter.readability.odd_characters.adv: Use standard fonts and simple bullets, then check the PDF by copying its text into a plain text editor.
recruiter.readability.fancy_bullets.advi: Prefer simple round bullets or dashes: some software turns symbols into odd characters.
recruiter.readability.filename_generic: The file name "{name}" does not say whose CV it is.
recruiter.readability.filename_generic.a: Rename the file as Name_Surname_CV, so it is easy to find among hundreds of attachments.
recruiter.readability.filename_version: The file name "{name}" contains a version or copy marker.
recruiter.readability.filename_version.a: Remove words like "final", "v2" or "(1)" from the file name.
recruiter.readability.filename_character: The file name "{name}" contains unusual characters or is very long.
Use only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores in the file name.
recruiter.career.total_years: About {years} years of work experience in total.
recruiter.career.no_dates: The work experience has no dates.
recruiter.career.no_dates.advice: Add start and end month and year to every job (for example 03/2019 - 06/2023).
recruiter.career.undated_roles: {count} role(s) appear to have no dates.
recruiter.career.undated_roles.advice: Give every role a start and end date: undated jobs look like something to hide.
recruiter.career.not_reverse_chronologic: The jobs are not in reverse chronological order.
List the most recent job first: recruiters and software expect it.
recruiter.career.reverse_chronological: Jobs are listed from the most recent.
recruiter.career.gap.advice: If you studied, trained, cared for family or travelled in that period, say so in one line.
recruiter.career.current_gap: No current job: the last one ended {months} months ago ({since}).
recruiter.career.current_gap.advice: Mention what you are doing now (courses, volunteering, freelance work) to show continuity.
recruiter.career.short_stints.advice: Explain short jobs briefly (fixed-term contract, project, company closure) so they do not look like quick exits.
recruiter.career.overlaps: {count} pair(s) of jobs overlap (up to {months} months).
recruiter.career.overlaps.advice: If the jobs were really in parallel, mark one as part-time; otherwise correct the dates.
recruiter.career.date_formats_mixed: Dates are written in different formats ({formats}).
recruiter.career.date_formats_mixed.advi: Use one format everywhere, preferably month/year (03/2021).
recruiter.career.dates_year_only.advice: Add the month too: "2019 - 2020" can mean two months or two years.
recruiter.substance.results_good: {share}% of the job descriptions contain numbers or results ({count} of {total}).
recruiter.substance.results_few: Only {share}% of the job descriptions contain numbers or results ({count} of {total}).
recruiter.substance.results_few.advice: Add facts a recruiter can check: how many people, clients, pieces, euros, percentages or how much time.
recruiter.substance.results_missing: None of the job descriptions contains numbers or results ({count} of {total}).
recruiter.substance.results_missing.advi: For each job add at least one concrete figure: team size, volumes, budget, savings, deadlines met.
recruiter.substance.descriptions_thin: Few description lines for your jobs ({lines} lines for {roles} roles).
recruiter.substance.descriptions_thin.ad: Give the recent jobs 2-4 lines each about tasks, tools and results.
recruiter.substance.descriptions_missing: Under each job write 2-4 lines on what you did, with which tools and with what result.
recruiter.substance.weak_openings: {count} lines ({share}%) start with weak phrases such as "responsible for".
recruiter.substance.weak_openings.advice: Start with what you did: "Managed", "Reduced", "Trained" instead of "Responsible for" or "Helped with".
recruiter.substance.weak_openings_few: {count} line(s) start with a weak phrase such as "responsible for".
recruiter.substance.weak_openings_few.ad: Rewrite those lines starting with an action and its result.
recruiter.substance.action_verbs: Most lines ({share}%) start with an action.
recruiter.substance.buzzwords.advice: Replace adjectives about yourself with facts that prove them: an example says more than "motivated" or "team player".
recruiter.substance.first_person: The CV uses the first person {count} times.
recruiter.substance.first_person.advice: In the job descriptions drop "I" and "my": start each line with the action.
recruiter.substance.first_person_few.adv: First person is fine in a short summary; avoid it in the job descriptions.
recruiter.substance.long_paragraphs.advi: Split long paragraphs into short bullet points that can be scanned in seconds.
recruiter.substance.repeated_word.advice: Vary the wording or merge the lines that repeat it.
recruiter.coverage.good: The CV shows {covered} of {total} essential skills of your occupation ({share}%).
recruiter.coverage.partial: The CV shows {covered} of {total} essential skills of your occupation ({share}%).
recruiter.coverage.partial.advice: If you have the missing skills, name them explicitly with an example: the software searches for the words.
recruiter.coverage.low: The CV shows only {covered} of {total} essential skills of your occupation ({share}%).
recruiter.coverage.low.advice: Check that the occupation is right; then describe the skills you really have with the words used in job ads.
recruiter.coverage.missing_skills.advice: Add only the skills you really have, each with a short concrete example.
recruiter.personal.birth_date: The CV shows your date of birth.
recruiter.personal.birth_date.advice: It is not needed to assess you and may invite age bias: you can remove it.
recruiter.personal.age.advice: Age is not needed and may invite bias: you can remove it.
recruiter.personal.marital_status: The CV mentions marital status or children.
recruiter.personal.marital_status.advice: Remove it: it is private and irrelevant to the job.
recruiter.personal.nationality: The CV mentions nationality or citizenship.
recruiter.personal.nationality.advice: Keep it only if it matters for the job (for example your right to work); otherwise you can remove it.
recruiter.personal.gender.advice: It is not needed in a CV: you can remove it.
recruiter.personal.tax_code: The CV contains an Italian tax code.
recruiter.personal.tax_code.advice: Remove it: it is a sensitive identifier that is only needed when you are hired.
recruiter.personal.full_address: The CV shows your full street address.
recruiter.personal.full_address.advice: The town is enough; a full address in a CV that circulates widely is unnecessary personal data.
recruiter.personal.photo: The CV appears to contain a photo.
recruiter.personal.photo.advice: Many recruiters prefer CVs without a photo to avoid bias; keep it only if it is customary in your sector or requested.
recruiter.personal.gdpr_present: The CV contains the consent to the processing of personal data.
recruiter.personal.gdpr_missing: No consent line for the processing of personal data.
recruiter.personal.gdpr_missing.advice: Not required by law, but many Italian recruiters expect it: you can add "Autorizzo il trattamento dei dati personali ai sensi del Regolamento UE 2016/679" at the bottom.
recruiter.hidden.text_invisible: The file contains invisible text ({count} line(s), {words} words).
recruiter.hidden.text_invisible.advice: Remove it: recruiters and modern software detect hidden keywords and usually discard the CV.
recruiter.hidden.text_white: The file contains white text on a white background ({count} line(s), {words} words).
recruiter.hidden.text_white.advice: Remove it: white keywords show up as soon as the text is copied or parsed and look like cheating.
recruiter.hidden.text_tiny: The file contains text in a tiny font ({count} line(s), {words} words).
recruiter.hidden.text_tiny.advice: Remove it or make it readable: microscopic text is treated as keyword stuffing.
recruiter.hidden.text_offpage: The file contains text placed outside the page ({count} line(s), {words} words).
recruiter.hidden.text_offpage.advice: Remove it: text outside the page is invisible to people but read by software, and is seen as a trick.
recruiter.hidden.repeated_term.advice: Name each skill once or twice, inside real examples: repetition looks like keyword stuffing.
recruiter.hidden.long_keyword_list: {count} line(s) contain lists of {items} or more keywords.
recruiter.hidden.long_keyword_list.advic: Keep the skills list short and grouped; show the important skills in the job descriptions.
recruiter.hidden.duplicated_block.advice: Remove the duplicates: repeated blocks look like an attempt to game the software.
recruiter.hidden.job_ad_text: {count} lines look copied from a job advertisement.
recruiter.hidden.job_ad_text.advice: Do not paste the job ad into the CV: describe in your own words how you meet its requirements.
recruiter.hidden.clean: No hidden text or keyword stuffing found.
ai.title: AI-style signals
ai.notice.limits: These are style cues, not a verdict. Tools that try to detect AI writing are unreliable, especially for non-native writers and for CVs that follow a template; nothing here says who wrote your CV. Use the cues to make your CV more personal and concrete.
ai.notice.unreliable: The text is too short for a meaningful reading ({words} words; at least {minimum} are needed).
ai.signal.stock_phrases: {count} stock phrases often found in AI-polished CVs ({per_100} per 100 words): {phrases}.
ai.signal.stock_phrases.advice: Replace stock phrases with specific facts: which company, which tool, which result, in which year.
ai.signal.uniformity: The {count} lines have very similar lengths (about {mean_words} words each; variation {variation}).
ai.signal.uniformity.advice: Real experience is uneven: let important points take more space and minor ones less.
ai.signal.result_clauses: {count} of {total} lines ({share}%) end with the same pattern "..., resulting in / ensuring ...".
ai.signal.result_clauses.advice: Vary the structure and keep only results you can explain in an interview.
ai.signal.metric_endings: {count} of {total} lines ({share}%) end with a figure.
ai.signal.metric_endings.advice: Figures are good, but make sure each is real and that you can tell how it was measured.
ai.signal.genericity: {count} of {total} lines ({share}%) contain no name, number, tool, place or date.
ai.signal.genericity.advice: Anchor each line to something concrete: the product, the software, the client type, the size of the team.
ai.signal.typography: Typographic habits common in generated text: {em_dashes} em dashes between words, {curly_quotes} pairs of curly quotes, {title_case_headings} headings in Title Case.
ai.signal.typography.advice: A weak cue: use the punctuation and capitalisation you normally use (in Italian, headings in sentence case).
ai.signal.embedding: {count} of {total} lines ({share}%) read very much like typical AI-style CV sentences.
ai.signal.embedding.advice: Rewrite those lines in your own words, with details only you could give.
ai.signal.metadata_ai_tool: The file metadata names an AI writing tool ({producer}).
ai.signal.metadata_ai_tool.advice: The metadata travels with the file; if you edited the text yourself, export it again from your word processor.
ai.signal.metadata_cv_builder: The file was produced by an online CV builder ({producer}).
ai.signal.metadata_cv_builder.advice: Not a problem in itself; just check that the template text was replaced with your own.

model_cause.runtime.advice: The scoring engine needs the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime, which is missing or damaged on this PC. Install it from Microsoft: https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe and start ReverseHire again.
model_cause.blocked.advice: Windows (Smart App Control or an application control policy) or the antivirus blocked a file of the scoring engine. In Windows Security, App & browser control, check Smart App Control, or allow the ReverseHire program folder in the antivirus, then start ReverseHire again.
model_cause.network.short: the model is not on this PC and could not be downloaded
model_cause.network.advice: The model files (about 470 MB) were not found in any model folder, and the download failed: no Internet connection, or a proxy blocks it. Connect to the Internet and start a new search, or copy the models folder of the installation media into the folder listed under Details.
model_cause.certificate.advice: The model is not on this PC and its download was refused because the website certificate was not trusted: usually the antivirus scans HTTPS connections, or a company proxy does. Allow ReverseHire (or huggingface.co) in the antivirus web protection, or copy the models folder of the installation media into the folder listed under Details.
model_cause.damaged.advice: The model files are incomplete or damaged (for example after an interrupted copy). Delete the model folder listed under Details and run the installation again, or start a search with the Internet on to download it again.
model_cause.memory.advice: There was not enough free memory (RAM) to load the model. Close other programs, lower "Companies in parallel" in tab 2, and start a new search.
model_cause.not_writable.short: the model folder cannot be written
model_cause.not_writable.advice: The model had to be downloaded, but its folder cannot be written (read-only, or blocked by the antivirus' controlled folder access). Allow ReverseHire in the antivirus, or copy the models folder of the installation media into the folder listed under Details.
model_cause.unknown.advice: The reason is not clear. Open the ? menu, Diagnostics, copy the result and send it together with the log file (? menu, Open log folder).

ai.rewrite.stock_phrases: Replace “{phrase}” with what you actually did: the task, the tool or method, and a result someone could check.
ai.rewrite.stock_phrases_generic: Replace the set phrase with what you actually did: the task, the tool or method, and a result someone could check.
ai.rewrite.uniformity: Vary this line: cut it to the essential fact, or add one detail (who, which tool, how many) so it does not read like its neighbours.
ai.rewrite.result_clauses: Split the clause after the comma: state the action first, then the result as its own short sentence, with a figure only if you can prove it.
ai.rewrite.metric_endings: Keep a number only where it is real and checkable; start the line with the most important fact instead of ending every line with a figure.
ai.rewrite.genericity: Anchor this line with something concrete: a name, a tool, a place, a number (for example the software, the type of customer or the size of the team).
ai.rewrite.typography: Replace the long dash (—) and the curly quotes with the plain punctuation you would type yourself.
ai.rewrite.embedding: This line reads like a stock template: say it in your own words, with one real example from your work.

rsim.profile.allibo.confidence: The parsing engine is not documented publicly: the simulation assumes the worst plausible case (linear reading, header and footer dropped, images lost, months required).
rsim.profile.allibo.note.ai: No AI ranking or semantic matching is documented publicly; 'screening support' against requirements, questionnaires, tests and video interviews are.
rsim.profile.allibo.note.dedup: Allibo documents CV deduplication: send one updated file per company, not variants under different e-mail addresses.
rsim.profile.allibo.note.form: The spontaneous-application form asks only name, e-mail, the CV file and up to two professional areas: the file is all the recruiter has.
rsim.profile.allibo.note.search: Recruiters search the archive with advanced keyword searches: put the role words of the area you choose and the exact technologies in the text.
rsim.profile.allibo.retention: Retention is set by each employer; one employer's privacy notice read in November 2026 states 6 months, extendable to 24 months, and says public LinkedIn profiles may also be read.
rsim.profile.arca24.confidence: Only marketing pages describe a multilingual semantic search engine; nothing technical was read.
rsim.profile.arca24.note.semantic: A semantic engine can match synonyms, but the recruiter still reads your exact words.
rsim.profile.ashby.confidence: The review marks each recruiter criterion as met or not met, with citations; decisions stay with humans per the vendor.
rsim.profile.ashby.note.criteria: Each criterion the recruiter sets is marked 'meets' or 'does not meet' with a quote from your CV: state each requirement you meet in plain words.
rsim.profile.baseline_literal.confidence: Not a real product: a conservative default for unknown platforms (linear reading, header and footer dropped, images lost, strict headings, literal whole-word search).
rsim.profile.baseline_literal.note.defau: Used for platforms we cannot recognise; the real system may be better or worse.
rsim.profile.baseline_literal.retention: Unknown platform: retention is stated in the employer's privacy notice.
rsim.profile.bullhorn.confidence: Release notes document ranked recommendations from the agency database and a configurable weighting of screening answers against resume match (50/50 by default).
rsim.profile.bullhorn.note.client: Ask which client the ad is for before agreeing to be presented.
rsim.profile.bullhorn.note.screen: The agency may screen you by chat or voice; screening answers and resume match are weighted together.
rsim.profile.bullhorn.retention: The agency keeps you in its database and may present you for later jobs.
rsim.profile.email_no_ats.confidence: A person opens the file: nothing is parsed or scored automatically, but the first skim is short.
rsim.profile.email_no_ats.note.pdf: Send a PDF named with your name, and write the role in the e-mail subject.
rsim.profile.email_no_ats.note.skim: A first skim is short: your current title, employer, dates and top skills must be visible in the first third of page one.
rsim.profile.email_no_ats.retention: The company's privacy notice states how long it keeps e-mailed CVs.
rsim.profile.greenhouse.confidence: The match-score add-on is documented; the vendor says it does not reject automatically. Parsing details are not documented.
rsim.profile.greenhouse.note.reject: The vendor states that Talent Matching does not advance or reject candidates by itself.
rsim.profile.icims.confidence: Candidate ranking with Job Fit tiers is documented as an add-on; the method is not.
rsim.profile.icims.note.fit: Recruiters may see a Job Fit tier: the requirement words of the posting count.
rsim.profile.inrecruiting.confidence: Job Matching percentages, tag-based suggested candidates and anonymised CVs are documented in the help pages; the layout handling of the parser is not, so reading is simulated as linear.
rsim.profile.inrecruiting.note.blind: Blind selection may hide personal data from the recruiter.
rsim.profile.inrecruiting.note.suggested: Candidates can be found later through 'Suggested Candidates': keep the profile in your candidate area up to date.
rsim.profile.inrecruiting.note.tags: Inda parses the CV, fills the form and computes a match percentage from the vacancy tags: use the vacancy's own words.
rsim.profile.inrecruiting.retention: Retention depends on the employer; your profile stays in your InRecruiting candidate area.
rsim.profile.oracle.confidence: Only the titles of the documentation pages on disqualification and prescreening questions were read.
rsim.profile.oracle.note.questions: Disqualification questions can reject automatically; prescreening answers can be scored.
rsim.profile.personio.confidence: The screening agent and its 'AI signals' are documented; how they are computed is not.
rsim.profile.personio.note.format: The AI screening needs the CV as a PDF, an image or a Word file.
rsim.profile.rchilli.confidence: The help pages contradict each other on where per-skill months come from; the simulation counts months only when the CV states the skill inside a dated job.
rsim.profile.rchilli.note.skills: Search & Match weighs skill frequency, duration and recency: name each skill inside the job where you used it.
rsim.profile.rchilli.retention: Retention depends on the employer using the parser.
rsim.profile.recruitee.confidence: A 'Matching Assistant' is named by the vendor; nothing about its method was read.
rsim.profile.recruitee.note.matching: The matching assistant compares your CV with the job: use the posting's own words for the skills you have.
rsim.profile.smartrecruiters.confidence: Only the High/Medium/Low match label is documented; parsing and search details are not.
rsim.profile.smartrecruiters.note.winsto: Winston Match shows recruiters a High/Medium/Low label in the applicant list.
rsim.profile.staffing_agency_it.confiden: The agencies' back-office systems are not documented publicly; the simulation assumes a keyword search of the agency database and a phone screening.
rsim.profile.staffing_agency_it.note.cli: The ad names the agency, not the client: ask which client it is before agreeing to be presented.
rsim.profile.staffing_agency_it.note.tow: Agency recruiters search by role, skills and town: write your town in the CV header.
rsim.profile.staffing_agency_it.retentio: Agencies keep candidates in their own database for later searches.
rsim.profile.successfactors.confidence: Required, scored and disqualifier prescreening questions are documented in SAP knowledge-base articles; the parser is a partner product.
rsim.profile.successfactors.note.disqual: A question flagged 'disqualifier' rejects a wrong answer automatically; scored answers feed the candidate rating. Answer truthfully.
rsim.profile.teamtailor.confidence: A CV summary matched against the job description and screening by criteria are documented; the method is not.
rsim.profile.teamtailor.note.summary: Recruiters may read an automatic summary of your CV next to the job description: make the first lines state your role and main skills.
rsim.profile.textkernel.confidence: The parser output and its Resume Quality codes are documented in detail; which employer uses which settings is not.
rsim.profile.textkernel.note.columns: Columnar layouts are a fatal quality code (433): use one column.
rsim.profile.textkernel.note.contact: Contact details not at the top (311), missing job dates (419) and vertical date ranges (418) are quality codes.
rsim.profile.textkernel.note.months: The parser computes months of experience without double counting, average months per employer, and months plus last-used date per skill.
rsim.profile.textkernel.retention: Retention depends on the employer using the parser.
rsim.profile.workable.confidence: A match score and requirement checklist per candidate are documented; their method is not.
rsim.profile.workable.note.score: Recruiters see a match score and a requirement checklist next to your name.
rsim.profile.workday.confidence: The A-D grade with fit and gap per requirement is documented by the vendor; the grading model itself is not public, so our embedder stands in for it.
rsim.profile.workday.note.grade: Top grades can be fast-tracked by the employer.
rsim.profile.workday.note.manual: Prefer 'Apply manually' and check every auto-filled field before submitting.

analysis.compare.help_text:
Simulated score: how well your CV would do in each system, always as 0–100 %, so you can compare the systems and sort them. It is an estimate from public documentation, not the real system.

How this system shows you: what the recruiter actually sees on that system. Some show letters A–D, some stars out of 5, some a band (High / Medium / Low), and some no score at all, only how many must-have requirements you meet. Point at a cell to read its scale.
